newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iberia wants to head European alliance.
newsitem.headline: Iberia wants to head European alliance.

text.p: Spanish state airline Iberia wants to head a European alliance made up of KLM, Swissair and Alitalia, chairman Xabier de Irala said in an interview published on Monday.

"Iberia is a company which, in this process of globalisation and of concentration we are living, has no future if it tries to survive by itself," Irala told the financial daily Gaceta de los Negocios.
"According to analysts, there will be three or four groups left in Europe whose leaders seem clear: British Airways, Lufthansa and Air France, if the latter manages to solve its problems," he said.

"Iberia's alternative is either joining one of these groups or forming part of a fourth alliance with KLM, possibly with Swissair and also with Alitalia," Irala said. "We would be the biggest group in Europe if that happened."
"We would like to head that project, with the permission of KLM," he added.

Irala said Iberia could not continue alone because it was relatively small and did not have a market niche. "I am convinced, and I will defend this, that the strategy depends on one or more alliances," he said.
The strong points of the company were its leadership position in the domestic and South American markets and the enormous development potential of Madrid's Barajas airport.
"Madrid is going to become a very important European hub and large foreign companies are very aware of this," he said.
Irala said negotiations with KLM were at an advanced stage and he hoped the outlook would be clearer within two months.
